newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: Petrovietnam confirms president changed in shuffle.
newsitem.headline: Petrovietnam confirms president changed in shuffle.

text.p: State-owned Vietnam Oil and Gas Corp (Petrovietnam) confirmed on Wednesday that Ho Sy Thoang has been replaced as president and chief executive officer and appointed chairman of the management board in a major reshuffle.

Vu Van Mao, Director of Petrovietnam's Information Centre, said Thoang would be replaced by Ngo Thuong San, Director of VietSovPetro, a Vietnamese-Russian joint venture which is the country's biggest oil producer.
The changes would take effect from October 1, he told Reuters after a preview of Vietnam's Third International Oil and Gas Exhibition to be held in Ho Chi Minh City from March 26 to 28.
Mao said the changes were necessary to allow Thoang to take over as chairman of the management board, a position vacated in May by Finance Minister Ho Te.
Other changes included the appointment of Nguyen Thi Ngoc Suong, a vice president in charge of commerce and finance, to the management board, Mao said.
She would be replaced by Hoang Van Hoan, Petrovietnam's specialist in government affairs.

Two additional vice presidents will also be appointed to assist the president. Tran Ngoc Canh, currently general manager for exploration and production, will take charge of production and development. Nguyen Xuan Nham, currently managing director for technical services, is the other.
Petrovietnam currently has three other vice presidents -- Nguyen Tri Lien, Nguyen Hiep and Tran Hien.

A Reuters report on Monday cited western oil industry executives as saying the reshuffle could reflect government frustration over hitches which have marred the image of Vietnam's oil business as an emerging energy frontier.

Next year's oil and gas exhibition is aimed at creating favourable conditions for major manufacturers and suppliers of oil and gas equipment and for heads of oil companies to meet Vietnamese decision makers, Mao said.

The organisers aimto attract 250 exhibitors from 20 countries to an event which will also include natural gas, refinery and petrochemical exhibitions as well as an oil and gas summit of top industry leaders.
